title: China AI Video Startup Kling Picks Banks for $1 Billion-Plus IPO
source_used: The Standard (HK) (https://www.thestandard.com.hk/finance/article/344723/Kuaishous-Kling-AI-eyes-US1b-HK-IPO-next-year-Bloomberg-reports), Investing.com on Yahoo Finance UK and Briefs Finance, all relaying Bloomberg. Bloomberg page itself blocked (HTTP 403).
key_facts: Bloomberg reported on 6 Oct 2026, citing people familiar, that Kling AI, the AI video platform of Kuaishou Technology, has selected banks for a Hong Kong IPO that could raise at least $1 billion.
Kling is working with China International Capital Corp, Goldman Sachs and UBS on the potential share sale and is targeting a listing as soon as next year.
Discussions remain ongoing and the size and timing of the offering could change.
Kling, launched in 2024, raised $2.8 billion in July from investors including Alibaba, Tencent and Baidu, at a value of about $15 billion before the new money.
Kuaishou's shares rose by as much as 3.5% in Hong Kong trading on Tuesday (The Standard; Briefs).
Rivals include ByteDance's Seedance and the start-ups Shengshu and PixVerse; Bloomberg has reported that both start-ups are also pursuing Hong Kong listings (Briefs).
In May, The Information reported that Kuaishou had been eyeing a 2027 IPO for the platform (Briefs).
quote_evidence: Kling AI is working with China International Capital Corp, Goldman Sachs and UBS Group on the potential listing and is targeting to go public in the city as soon as next year, the report said.
Discussions remain ongoing and the size and timing of the offering could change, Bloomberg reported.
In July, it secured $2.8 billion from investors such as Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Tencent Holdings Ltd. and Baidu Inc., valuing the company at roughly $15 billion before new money.
why_it_matters_hint: Another Chinese AI company is lining up a Hong Kong listing, this time in AI video, where the field is crowded.
notes: Bloomberg's page could not be opened; facts read in The Standard (HK), Investing.com and Briefs Finance, all relaying Bloomberg's report. Briefs' market commentary is not used.
